title: Expand buffer cache and align planner I/O costs to cut physical reads
configuration_cause: shared_buffers=16384 (128MB) is far below the 2TB host memory; blks_read_per_txn=1.51 vs blks_hit_per_txn=9.23 gives a low buffer hit ratio, and random_page_cost=4.0 overprices cached random reads, inflating physical I/O and terminal occupancy of GetUserTweets (88.5% of terminal capacity).
mechanism: The dominant transaction GetUserTweets consumes 88.5% of finite client terminal time, and per-transaction evidence shows 1.51 physical block reads against 9.23 buffer hits, i.e. a low buffer hit ratio. Raising shared_buffers retains more of the read working set; raising effective_cache_size and effective_io_concurrency lets the planner and executor exploit that cache and prefetch; lowering random_page_cost and seq_page_cost together keeps their ratio sane while favoring cached index/random access. Fewer physical reads shorten per-transaction service time, freeing terminal capacity and raising completed-transaction goodput.
query_effect: GetUserTweets and GetFollowers should resolve more blocks from shared buffers, reducing physical reads and per-query service time.
expected_tps_effect: Increase completed-transaction TPS as terminal capacity is freed by shorter GetUserTweets service times.
expected_latency_effect: Decrease GetUserTweets p95 and overall p95.

predictions.rationale: Larger cache plus cache-favoring planner costs reduce physical reads.
Fewer physical reads shorten the dominant transaction's tail.
Freed terminal capacity raises completed goodput.

alternatives.statement: If the working set already fits and reads are not the bottleneck, blks_read_per_txn stays flat and TPS is unchanged; then WAL commit-path tuning is the better lever.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves the mandatory buffer_cache_capacity bundle untested despite an active low_buffer_hit_ratio alert and 1.51 physical reads per transaction; a coherent cache+planner action directly targets the dominant transaction's I/O.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x current 128MB to 512MB, within safe range 8192-65536; host has 2TB RAM so ample headroom.
Double planner cache estimate to 8GB, within 131072-1048576.
Raise prefetch concurrency from 1 to 16, within 0-256.
Lower cached random read cost from 4.0 to 1.5, within 1.0-6.0.
Slightly lower I/O cost scale to 0.8, within 0.5-2.0, preserving ratio with random_page_cost.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost

edges.relation: raises cache retention and lowers planner I/O cost
fewer physical reads shorten dominant transaction

cross_domain_requirements: WAL commit-path tuning (wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay, commit_delay) remains a separate competing mechanism for the wal_wait alert.
